newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products mixed with crude falls.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products mixed with crude falls.

text.p: Singapore oil products were steady to lower on Friday on crude falls with gas oil traders having mixed views on India's diesel tender for February.

India was expected to take between 500,000 and over 700,000 tonnes of diesel in its tender with most offers based on high of Mediterranean quotes, reflecting better arbitrage opportunities there compared with the MidEast. But some traders expected India to take below 500,000 tonnes, prompting swaps prices to dip in late afternoon. January swaps rose in active early trading at $32.30-$32.45, but slipped to $31.80-$31.95 in the evening, compared with $32.20-$32.24 barrel on Thursday,

Sellers said they were willing to sell gas oil at 55 cents a barrel over Singapore quotes fob but a bid was seen at a low 20 cents premium for mid-January. A major offered a 30,000-tonne gas oil cargo for Jan 9-13 lifting at $32.70, fob below Thursday's offers of $32.80-$33.00. A physical deal into China was heard done at $255 a tonne c+f, reflecting current firm levels. Traders said Japan's kerosene demand remained steady for mid-January arrival but a deal was done at a lower premium of $2.20 a barrel over Singapore quotes c+f compered with $2.30-$2.40 previously. Jet fuel was offered slightly lower to $33 for mid-January lifting, compared with $33.55 on Thursday.

Gasoline and naphtha were steady in a dull market. Swaps were largely unchanged from Thursday with January naphtha quoted at $24.10/$24.20, gasoline bid at $25.20 per barrel. Although gasoline was on the long side in Singapore in January, some traders said gasoline was underpriced. Others said the gasoline/ naphtha spread was due to narrow, taking the lead from Europe where regular unleaded gasoline was $9 a tonne below naphtha. But majors still assessed gasoline cargoes at $1.00-$1.20 a barrel over naphtha quotes.
Fuel oil slipped $1.00 in late trading as the full impact of the crude fall was felt.--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3084)
